title: Phase 1B: Identical-geometry comparison (xTB R/TS/P frozen)
purpose: Eliminate path-search methodology by evaluating both xTB and MACE on the exact same three geometries (native xTB reactant, TS, product). Determine whether the energetic disagreement persists when both see identical structures.

TS.method: xTB native --path search + Sella refinement + Hessian verification

xTB_reference_values.comment: From FINDINGS_diels_alder.md; verified concerted scan + Sella + Hessian
xTB_reference_values.TS_verified_by: Sella saddle optimization from relaxed scan guess; Hessian shows exactly one imaginary mode

TS_force_norm_eV_per_Angstrom.xTB_comment: Should be near zero at a true TS

barrier_heights_on_identical_geometries.interpretation: MACE sees a higher (27.9 vs 6.7) barrier than xTB when both evaluate the same frozen R/TS/P geometries. The disagreement is NOT explained by path methodology; it is a fundamental PES difference.

reaction_energies_on_identical_geometrie.interpretation: MACE predicts less exothermic products than xTB on the same geometries.

critical_finding_TS_stationarity.interpretation: The xTB TS is a true saddle point on the xTB PES (fmax ~0.0009), but it is NOT a saddle point on the MACE PES. MACE has substantial residual forces (~1.84 eV/Å) at this geometry, indicating it is not even close to a MACE saddle. The xTB TS must be optimized/searched on the MACE PES to find the actual MACE saddle.

summary.question: Is the MACE-xTB barrier disagreement explained by path-search methodology differences?
summary.answer: NO. When both potentials evaluate the exact same frozen R/TS/P geometries, they still show large disagreements: barrier 27.9 (MACE) vs 6.7 (xTB) kcal/mol, and reaction energy -36.2 (MACE) vs -57.6 (xTB) kcal/mol. The disagreement is a genuine PES difference, not a path artifact.
summary.additional_finding: The xTB TS is not stationary on the MACE PES (MACE fmax 1.84 eV/Å at this geometry). A MACE-native saddle search must be run to locate the true MACE transition state. The NEB barrier of ~36 kcal/mol may be measuring a different TS location or carrying residual forces from the algorithm's difficulty with xTB's flat surface.
summary.next_phase: Phase 1C will use the xTB TS as an initial guess for a MACE saddle-point search (Sella) to find the true MACE TS and answer whether it is nearby the xTB TS or elsewhere on the PES.
